offence_severity: Life imprisonment and fine of Rs.5,000/- each under Sections 302 and 1208, and two years RI and fine of Rs.1,000/- each under Section 201 IPC
physical_harm: Various grievous injuries on the neck and scalp, multiple fractures on the skull
number_of_offences: Charged under Sections 302, 1208 and 201 IPC; convictions under Sections 302, 1208 and 201 IPC
premeditation_planning: The court found premeditation/planning as the accused had an opportunity to commit the murder and there was a conspiracy among the accused, co-accused and the deceased's wife
motive: The appellant had a grudge on account of the marriage of Sudesh Rani with the deceased
key_evidence_accepted: The chain of all the circumstantial evidence is complete and no link is missing and the accused persons had an opportunity to commit the murder of the deceased. The last seen theory was applied as the time gap between the last seen of the deceased and the discovery of the body was very small.
witness_credibility: The court acknowledged minor discrepancies in the depositions of the witnesses and the inquest report, but held that such discrepancies do not affect the core of the prosecution case and that the credibility of the witnesses should be assessed based on the entire evidence.

legal_representation.state: Nupur Choudhary, Samir Ali Khan, Sanjay Jain

investigation_status: FIR lodged, charge sheet filed, trial completed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused and co-accused killed the deceased at the instance of deceased's wife and threw away the body in the canal. There was a conspiracy among the accused, co-accused, and the deceased's wife to do away with the deceased. The accused and co-accused were convicted under sections 302, 1208, and 201 IPC and sentenced accordingly by the courts below.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there could be no motive for the appellant to commit the offence. They contended that the courts below committed an error in applying the last seen theory due to the long gap between the last seen and the recovery of the dead body. They also claimed that the recovery of incriminating material was not proved in accordance with law and that no independent witness had been examined.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the last seen theory comes into play only in a case where the time gap between the point of time when the accused and the deceased were seen alive and when the deceased was found dead is small. The court also considered the credibility of witness statements and the admissibility of evidence despite minor discrepancies.
precedent_relied_upon: Shankar v. State of Karnataka AIR 2011 SC 2302; State of Rajasthan v. Rajendra Singh AIR 1998 SC 2554; State Represented by Inspector of Police v. Saravanan AIR 2009 SC 152; Arumugam v. State, AIR 2009 SC 331; Mahendra Pratap Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2009) 11 SCC 334; Vijay alias Chinee v. State of M.P. (2010) 8 SCC 191; State of U. P. v. Naresh & Ors. (2011) 4 SCC 324; Brahm Swaroop v. State of U.P. AIR 2011 SC 280; Dr. Sunil Kumar Sambhudayal Gupta v. State of Maharashtra (2010) 13 SCC 657; Atluri Brahmanandam (D) Thr. LRs. v. Anne Sai Bapuji AIR 2011 SC 545; Laxmibai (dead) Thr. L.Rs. & Anr. v. Bhagwantbuva (dead) Thr. L.Rs. & Ors, AIR 2013 SC 1204
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the chain of circumstantial evidence was complete, no link was missing, and the accused had an opportunity to commit the murder. The courts below correctly held the accused guilty of the offences.
